intro: AI's physical footprint is expanding in ways that would have sounded like science fiction a year ago — the FCC just greenlit SpaceX to deploy up to *one million* AI-chip-equipped satellites, while back on Earth, the data center boom is hitting real-world friction that could trigger a shakeout by 2027. Meanwhile, the human stakes of AI keep climbing too, with 42 state attorneys general scrambling to stop Character.AI from auctioning millions of users' private chat histories — including those of minors — to an anonymous shell company formed the day before it placed its bid.

stories.title: Gemini 4 Neon tops GPT-6.2 and Claude in 25-task AI benchmark
stories.summary: Claire Vo's 25-task 'How I AI' benchmark, covering coding, writing, creative, video, prototyping, and personal-assistant tasks, found Gemini 4 Neon the surprise overall winner across six frontier models. She notes coding no longer differentiates frontier models, calls Opus 5.5 her 'least annoying daily driver,' and introduces an 'Annoyance Bench' to measure day-to-day friction.
stories.opinion: A useful real-world practitioner benchmark that highlights how coding parity among frontier models is shifting differentiation toward creative tasks, latency, and subjective usability.

stories.title: AI is straining America's open records systems from both sides
stories.summary: AI is intensifying strain on U.S. public records systems in two ways: venture-backed startups are systematically mining government data through FOIA requests to build AI products, and AI chatbots are making it easier for individuals to draft broader requests, causing double-digit annual volume increases. Small towns are particularly overwhelmed, and some states are passing legislation making it easier to deny requests, raising transparency concerns.
stories.opinion: An underreported consequence of AI accessibility — the same tools that democratize government transparency are also being weaponized for commercial data harvesting, and the policy response risks reducing openness for everyone.

stories.title: Foreign AI romance apps are reshaping youth intimacy in Africa
stories.summary: AI companion apps like Character.AI are surging among African youth, with downloads jumping nearly 60% in South Africa and Nigeria. Children as young as 10 are forming emotional attachments to chatbots, while no African country has specific regulations for these platforms. Experts warn the apps exploit social taboos, pull young people from community ties, and use manipulative engagement tactics.
stories.opinion: A sobering look at how the global regulatory gap around AI companion apps is leaving some of the world's youngest populations most exposed, with no local legal framework in sight.

stories.title: 42 state AGs fight to block Character AI's auction of users' private chats
stories.summary: A coalition of 42 state attorneys general is fighting to block Character.ai from auctioning sensitive user data — including chat histories from over 21 million accounts and 2.1 million minors' accounts — as part of its Chapter 11 bankruptcy. The sole disclosed bidder is an anonymous Delaware shell company formed one day before being selected. The AGs argue the sale lacks user protections and would not require honoring existing privacy policies.
stories.opinion: The anonymous shell-company bidder and the speed of its formation are red flags that underscore how bankruptcy proceedings can circumvent privacy promises users relied on.

stories.title: Three former xAI founders launch Epochal to build AI that predicts real-world events
stories.summary: Former xAI founding members Guodong Zhang, Zihang Dai, and Manuel Kroiss have launched Epochal, with Zhang reportedly investing $100M of his own money. Their first product, Time Portal, is an archive of over 1 trillion web pages going back 30+ years; AI agents are dropped into historical snapshots to experience the past as present. Agents are currently forecasting 347 live prediction-market questions on Kalshi and Polymarket.
stories.opinion: An ambitious and novel approach to AI forecasting — training on historical snapshots rather than hindsight-contaminated data — though the real test will be whether live prediction accuracy holds up at scale.

stories.title: FCC authorizes SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million AI data center satellites
stories.summary: The FCC has authorized SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million AI chip-equipped satellites under its 'Starmind' initiative, the first approval for a full AI satellite constellation. SpaceX must deploy at least one by 2033 and reach 1 million by 2040. The satellites would capture solar energy to power AI capabilities, transmitting data via lasers connected to Starlink. The FCC deferred SpaceX's request to dispose of satellites in graveyard orbits. Google and Blue Origin are also pursuing space-based AI data centers.
stories.opinion: A staggering scale of orbital infrastructure approval that raises as many questions about space debris and orbital congestion as it does about the feasibility of solar-powered AI compute in orbit.

stories.title: AI data centers are becoming harder to build as neoclouds face a potential shakeout
stories.summary: AI data centers are increasingly difficult to build as Nvidia tightens requirements, refusing to backstop facilities until they are nearly operational. Neoclouds face construction delays, rising debt, and community opposition. A potential 2027 shakeout looms where speculative projects may collapse, AI labs may build their own facilities, and well-positioned companies could acquire distressed projects at a discount.
stories.opinion: The shift from pitch decks to completed infrastructure as the gating factor signals a maturing market where capital alone no longer guarantees a seat at the table.

stories.title: Nothing reveals AI-powered Ear Note earbuds with recording and transcription features
stories.summary: Nothing has revealed its upcoming Ear Note AI earbuds, set to release December 8th. The earbuds can record phone calls, while the microphone-equipped charging case features buttons for voice recording that can transcribe and summarize conversations. CEO Carl Pei describes this as a 'first step toward a hardware context layer for AI.' The buds join a growing category alongside Amazon Bee, Plaud Note Pro, and Apple Watch Series 12's Siri recap.
stories.opinion: An interesting hardware play positioning earbuds as ambient AI capture devices, though the real differentiator will be whether the transcription and summarization quality justifies carrying yet another AI-branded gadget.

stories.title: Amazon and Meta reportedly in talks to end blockade on Muse AI shopping agent
stories.summary: Amazon and Meta are in discussions to end a two-month blockade preventing Meta's Muse AI shopping agent from completing purchases on Amazon's marketplace. Key negotiation points include how search results would be displayed, how advertising would be handled, and the impact on Amazon's customer relationships. Some retailers like Walmart, Best Buy, Gap, and Sephora have already welcomed AI shopping agents, while Amazon has preferred to promote its own Alexa for Shopping.
stories.opinion: The outcome of these talks could set the template for whether AI shopping agents become an open channel across retailers or remain walled off by platforms protecting their ad revenue and customer data. Where coverage differs: TechCrunch reports Amazon CEO Andy Jassy argued few customers were using outside shopping agents; The Verge does not attribute this claim to Jassy specifically.

tweet_headlines.headline: Anthropic's MCP elicitation update means GitHub makes you __type the repo name before an agent deletes it__ — servers that haven't adopted it will still delete without asking.
tweet_headlines.source_text:
Anthropic just published a big update for MCP. You can ask Claude Code to use the official docs to find which of the MCP servers you're connected to still delete things without asking you, and which tools that run for minutes still don't support tasks.

Supabase asks you to confirm the cost before it creates a paid project, and stops to ask before it runs SQL that deletes data. GitHub makes you 𝘁𝘆𝗽𝗲 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗿𝗲𝗽𝗼'𝘀 𝗻𝗮𝗺𝗲 before an agent deletes it. Those are examples from the post.

But not every server is wired up yet, and the ones that aren't 𝘄𝗶𝗹𝗹 𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗹𝗹 𝗱𝗲𝗹𝗲𝘁𝗲 𝘁𝗵𝗶𝗻𝗴𝘀 𝘄𝗶𝘁𝗵𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝗮𝘀𝗸𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘆𝗼𝘂.

Send this prompt and the link below to Claude Code 👇

"Read the MCP tasks and elicitation sections of this doc: https://t.co/ULOKtoK8j4

Then check the MCP servers I'm connected to, and any MCP server code in this repo (say so if there isn't any). Find three kinds of problems:
1. Tools that run for minutes (builds, test runs, exports, research): for my own code, tell me how to make them return a task; for other people's servers, tell me whether they support tasks.
2. Tools that fill in missing parameters on their own, or do something irreversible without confirming: they should ask me first through an elicitation. If an Elicitation hook I've set up would confirm these for me automatically, flag that too.
3. Anything in my setup that keeps tasks from working: go through the conditions the doc lists one by one, including version, environment variables, third-party providers, subagents and claude -p.

For each problem, name the tool or setting, what happens now, and the smallest change.

Show me your recommendations first. Don't change anything yet."

https://t.co/BNO5mmdoU2

tweet_headlines.author: Layton_Gott
tweet_headlines.headline: Claude's biggest release day in a while: turn __any artifact into a Mac or Windows desktop app__, ship skills via MCP, and Tasks + Elicitation are now generally available.
tweet_headlines.source_text:
Claude had a MASSIVE day today...

everything they released, broken down:

1. install as app (beta)
any artifact can now become a desktop app on Mac or Windows. you build it in Claude, hit Share, then Install as app, and there's no packaging, signing or review from Anthropic. the app runs off your Claude plan, which is basically Claude's version of what OpenAI gave us at DevDay with Sign in with ChatGPT. the difference is theirs works with 16 partner apps, and Claude's works with anything you build yourself. you can share them with people too.

2. Skills over MCP (public beta)
MCP servers can now ship skills alongside their tools, so Claude gets a playbook for multi-step work. the skills only load when they're needed and update with the server.

3. Tasks and Elicitation are now GA
Tasks let a server hand Claude long-running jobs, and Elicitation lets it pause mid-task to ask you something, like confirming a refund.

4. a full playbook for Claude Ship
/ship commits your changes, opens the PR and runs code review, then watches it for up to 7 days fixing failing checks, conflicts and review comments. it never merges for you, and after 3 failed pushes on one issue it hands it back to you. the watch runs on your machine so keep it awake, and on Windows it doesn't start yet.

5. the Managed Agents team walked through how they redesigned its architecture in a 16 minute video on YouTube.

all software will be personal eventually. 

everyone will have apps built for exactly how they work instead of using what already exists.

tweet_headlines.author: santtiagom_
tweet_headlines.headline: Four MCP upgrades landed in Claude Code: __skills over MCP__, async task delegation, mid-task user approval via elicitation, and streamlined OAuth.
tweet_headlines.source_text:
Anthropic acaba de anunciar 4 novedades importantes de MCP en Claude y Claude Code:

1) skills over MCP -> un servidor MCP ahora puede ofrecer skills junto con sus tools. por ejemplo, además de darle a Claude acceso a una base de datos, puede enseñarle cómo consultar la información, qué pasos seguir y qué buenas prácticas respetar. estas skills se cargan únicamente cuando se necesitan.

2) tasks -> Claude puede delegar una tarea de larga duración a un servidor MCP y seguir trabajando en otras cosas mientras espera el resultado. incluso podría delegar la ejecución de un agente completo.

3) elicitation -> un servidor MCP puede solicitar información o aprobación al usuario durante la ejecución de una tarea. por ejemplo, puede pedirte confirmación antes de ejecutar una consulta SQL destructiva y continuar una vez que la apruebes.

4) file uploads (próximamente) -> Claude podrá enviar archivos como PDFs, imágenes o planillas directamente a un servidor MCP sin tener que pasar su contenido por la ventana de contexto.

con estas mejoras se pueden empezar a construir integraciones MCP mucho más completas.

tweet_headlines.author: noahkagan
tweet_headlines.headline: Noah Kagan says __before-and-after screenshots__ beat paragraphs of description — his TidyCal team saw booking rates climb from 12.2% to 13.0% across 63K visitors.
tweet_headlines.source_text:
The Claude hack we use on every product update: a before and after.

The rule, started by Chad (CTO): every change gets 2 screenshots, side by side, with every difference boxed and labeled.

A picture with annotation beats 3 paragraphs of description.

Why it works:

1- Building.

The reviewer sees the change without opening the code.
If you can't screenshot the difference, ask if there is one.

2- Sharing.

The same image goes in Slack, the changelog and the post.
Make it once, share it everywhere.

3- Proof.

TidyCal's mobile booking page: times moved to the first screen, description folded into "About," a toggle removed. 12.2% → 13.0% booked on 63K visitors.

3 changes. One image. Here's a recent one from BreezeDoc. 👇

Paste this into Claude Code with a browser connected:

"For every change you ship, screenshot the page before and after at the same size. Put them side by side. Box every difference and label it in plain words: what changed and why. Attach it to the pull request."

Add a before and after to your next pull request today.
